findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization is wired up with hardcoded empty data instead of the actual table result
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and a `tableData` whose `data` and `meta.fields/units` are all empty, instead of forwarding `result.data` / `result.meta` / the per-query field map from the surrounding `tableResults.map((result, i) => ...)` block. Consequence: any org with the flag turned on will see every dashboard table widget render with no columns and no rows, regressing table rendering for that org. The diff is replacing the `StyledSimpleTableChart` invocation that previously received `metadata={result.meta}`, `data={result.data}`, `fieldHeaderMap={datasetConfig.getFieldHeaderMap?.(widget.queries[i])}` and `getCustomFieldRenderer`; those need to be plumbed through to the new component (e.g. a `TabularData` built from `result.data` and `result.meta`) or the feature-flag branch must be removed until that plumbing exists.

findings.title: useFeedbackSummary dereferences data.summary / data.numFeedbacksUsed without checking data is defined
findings.body: The hook returns `{ summary: data.summary, ... tooFewFeedbacks: data.numFeedbacksUsed === 0 && !data.success }` after only guarding on `isPending` and `isError`. When `user-feedback-ai-summaries` is off (or `normalizedDateRange` is falsy), `enabled` is false so react-query never fetches and `data` is `undefined` while `isPending` is false and `isError` is false. Reaching the final return then throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'summary')` on every render of the consumer `FeedbackSummary`, which means the page crashes for any org that does not have the feature flag before the feature-flag check inside the consumer ever runs. Guard the final return on `data`, or add an explicit early-return for the `!data` branch.

findings.title: get_environment_info swallows every exception with logger.info, hiding real errors
findings.body: `get_environment_info` does `except Exception as e:` and then calls `logger.info("get_environment_info.no-environment", extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e})`. Two issues: (1) catching bare `Exception` masks unrelated bugs (e.g. a coding error in `get_recommended_event` or `get_environment`); narrowing to `Group.DoesNotExist` / `Environment.DoesNotExist` / `Event.DoesNotExist` would still handle the documented case while letting other failures surface; (2) using `logger.info` for an error path will not show up as an error in alerting; this should be `logger.warning` or `logger.exception` so that unexpected failures are visible.

findings.title: computeEmptyBucketsForSeries divides by zero when values array is empty
findings.body: `computeEmptyBucketsForSeries` does `Math.floor((emptyBucketsForSeries / series.values.length) * 100)` without guarding against an empty `series.values`. When called on a `TimeSeries` with no points, this returns `NaN`, which then propagates into the `empty_buckets_percentage` analytics payload and into the confidence footer. Add an early return `if (!series.values.length) return 0;` (or similar) before the division.

findings.title: columnOrder fallback crashes with TypeError when tableData is undefined
findings.body: When `columns` is not provided, the fallback does `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields).map(...)`. Because of `?.`, `tableData?.meta.fields` evaluates to `undefined` if `tableData` is undefined, and `Object.keys(undefined)` throws `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object`. Although the prop is typed required, the optional chaining shows the author assumed `tableData` could be absent (e.g. the loading path), but the access is not actually guarded. Either short-circuit on `tableData` being undefined (`return columns ?? []`) or guard `Object.keys((tableData?.meta?.fields) ?? {})` so the component does not throw in the empty-state / loading path.
